title: RAW_UNSCREENED: kain-Vierfeld aus q-Praefix und ol-Grenze
summary: RAW_UNSCREENED: f80v.32/.35 expose a literal 2x2 of kain with q present/absent and fused/split ol boundary; a compositional slot account predicts separable effects, while whole-word or line-template grammar predicts no stable factor effects.

design.scope_description: Only the exposed f77r, f80v and f85r1 paragraph lines in EXPOSED_PARAGRAPHS/RF_VARIANTS; f80v.30-.35 is the source-specific contrast and other pages are controls.
design.mechanism: A retained kain content head combines with two local written operators: q-presence and an ol boundary. Fused olkain and split ol kain are therefore distinct surface realizations of one slot family, with qol kain and qolkain supplying the q-present cells where written.
design.unit: Exact source-group tuples for f80v.30-.35: olkain, qolkain, qol kain, ol kain, plus qokain/kain controls on f77r and f85r1.
design.contrast: Independent q/ol compositional slot effects versus unrelated whole words or a paragraph-specific spacing/template grammar.
design.prediction: The compositional account predicts that the four observed cells retain kain as the same content head while q-presence and split/fused boundary each produce a repeatable local slot/configuration effect. It also predicts that this factorization should recur in at least one f77r or f85r1 kain-family control. A whole-word/line-template rival predicts no cross-cell factor consistency after exact position and neighbor controls.
concrete_observations: ZL/IT/RF f80v.35 contain qol kain (G006-G007) and ol kain (G009-G010), with RF definite spaces; the complete line is tol oltain olkar y qol qol kain okiin ol kain shey ldy.
f80v.32 contains qolkain in every reader; ZL has s olkain ... qolkain, while IT/RF have solkain ... qolkain (IT splits arol keedy; RF preserves raw boundaries).
f80v.30/.31/.33 independently repeat fused olkain, while f77r.23 and f85r1.4 contain olshedy qokeedy as non-kain boundary controls.
linked_consequences: Within f80v.35, qol kain versus ol kain should differ in the same q-conditioned way while preserving the kain head and its local neighbor class.

Across f80v.32 and the fused controls, qolkain versus olkain should show the corresponding q effect without silently treating spaces as errors; a second-page kain-family control is required before selection.
design.nearest_rival: qolkain, olkain, qol kain and ol kain are unrelated lexical or phrase-template units; spacing is a scribal/layout choice with no compositional role.
design.distinguishing_observation: Predeclare the four cells and score exact boundary, token count, and immediate neighbor/slot configuration from raw groups. A positive discriminator requires both q contrasts and boundary contrasts to reproduce under matched controls; recurrence of forms alone fails.
assumption_costs: kain is a retained content head
q and ol effects are separable
within-reader spacing can carry a relation
design.strongest_likely_failure: Only f80v supplies the full rectangle; neighbor configurations may be line-specific, and no second-page kain control may meet the predeclared requirement.
